cells.tense: You are here and open, and what enters is being met without a grip.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Name what you actually want most right now, before you can see its shape, then face it for a few minutes — enough to know you turned.
cells.core: You're standing at the edge where the outside becomes inside, and nothing has been decided about what's coming over it yet. Open, uncommitted, available. Not blank. Full, and unsplit. The clean way this goes is that you turn toward a wanted thing before you have worked out whether it's sensible — no hedging, no preview of how it'll look next month. The difference now is that the turn itself hasn't been made. Whatever is at the edge, you're watching it instead of facing it. Facing toward what you want, without knowing yet if you'll get it or how, is the whole movement today. The rest of that direction doesn't have to exist for the first step of it to be real.
cells.sheetLine: Face what you want before you know if it's sensible.
cells.verb: arriving before it has chosen what to become
cells.place: the threshold where what was outside crosses in

cells.tense: You will land on nothing, because every door is being held ajar at once.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Sign an act you've already done and not claimed — done once, no case made for it, nothing said about what it was for.
cells.core: Everything is still possible and nothing has landed. From outside it reads as someone full of what could be. It isn't that. It's a hover — held aloft so no commitment gets made, so no one has to see what actually got done. Keeping every option warm has a cost, and the cost is the ground you'd stand on if you chose. What's clean here is that what shows is just what you are, no proof attached. An act done, claimed, and set down unproved gives you that. It doesn't have to mean anything larger. It only has to be yours, standing there without a hand to explain it. What gets made stays made, and one door closes behind it.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping every door open so nothing has to land.
cells.verb: arriving before it has chosen what to become
cells.place: the threshold where what was outside crosses in

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, waiting for it to open.
cells.act: look at the same thing longer, until it shows you more
cells.ask: Stay with one thing past the first glance — no verdict, no trying to wrap it up. Let more looking happen and see what it turns up.
cells.core: What comes toward you gets met from a hallway, not from inside the room. Anything fresh resembles the fresh things that already turned out to be a door you walked through, so nothing new is being let in. That's the constriction, and it's been doing its old job. Reopening the door isn't the ask. Staying with one thing longer than a glance is. No conclusion owed, no verdict made, just more attention than usual given to something that's already here. Whatever a longer look would show gets shown. Looking starts moving again, and the closed door stops being the only fact in the hallway.
cells.sheetLine: The door's closed and you're still waiting at it.
cells.verb: arriving before it has chosen what to become
cells.place: the threshold where what was outside crosses in

cells.tense: You are writing in a room and answering what enters as conditions rather than choices.
cells.act: sketch the whole of it badly, on one page, and keep the sketch
cells.ask: Put the whole situation on one page as a rough sketch — fast, unpolished, kept. Don't revise it. Let it show what's actually there.
cells.core: Doors stand open and none of them register as doors. What arrives gets answered like conditions you didn't set, not like something you could meet, and it bends to fit whatever you were already doing. From inside, this doesn't feel like steering. It feels like a run of things happening to you, and not seeing a way out is old and familiar. The way through fog is a small light, enough for the next step. A bad sketch gives that. One page, quick, no tidying. It doesn't have to be right and it doesn't have to be finished. Getting it down on paper is the whole point, and once it's down, the way out has a shape.

attempts.check: The record supports that a person in this seat can be present with what's arriving, but I'm inferring they already know which thing is at the door — the record only says something is entering, not that it's named. A reader could reasonably say they don't know what's arriving or have already chosen. The asks survive being wrong because each is doable regardless of whether what's arriving is identified: turning toward one thing they want, doing something their own way, looking longer, sketching what's in front of them. The sentence serving the writer more than the person is any line implying a single unambiguous arrival already recognized.
